name: Geometry
description: buildings, creatures, characters, vehicles: anything 3D she builds
content:
# Geometry

Levels buy detail: parts branch on `ctx.lod` (1 every tassel and bevel, further than you would go without levels, 2 drops trim, 3 the big forms, 4 the outline boxes, 5 one closed hull); a script's own level whose smallest cube is c metres hands over at `c / ctx.view.pixel` metres. Levels keep outline and paint.

- Scale: a body is a 1.9 × 0.7 m capsule, eye 1.6: doors 1.1–1.3 × 2.2–2.4 m, ceilings 2.7–3.5, rooms ≥ 4 m, stairs 0.18 rise / 0.28 tread. One `light` per room: torch or hearth 20–40.
- Floor first: under the creator (`ctx.place.players`) before `terrain: kind: "off"` removes ground. Ground is prepared, never floated over: a `flatten` mark on the footprint (→heightmap-terrain), `ctx.groundY`, `ctx.groundNormal` per post. A tunnel is your tube round the camera.
- Frame: −Z forward, +Y up, origin where it attaches; a positive `pitch` tips the nose up; facing +Z or ±X, `forward: "+z"` in the `primitive`.
- Paint is a brush: `ctx.albedo("cdn/texture-limewash-plaster.png")` (any `texture-<subject>`) textures what follows until `ctx.albedo(null)`; realism textures every face; trees and bushes wear leaf sprays (→trees, →leaf-sprays). `ctx.color` over a texture tints by the linear value (L 0.6 ≈ ×0.2), so tint at L 0.9+ and darken a room with its lights. A texture script (`spawn api TextureScript`) paints pixels the game computes.
- `collider(ctx)` is only the shell a body touches: closed slabs or sheets, openings open; props meet a sheet from above either way, from below only on its CCW side, walkers from either; opaque faces draw both sides, never a second copy facing back.
- Script + params + seed = ONE mesh, shared by all naming it. A moving part (a door leaf) is its own `kinematic` or `dynamic` object carrying the joint (`ctx.self.joints`). A road is one route spelled twice: a `road` mark's `spline` grades the ground, a `scripted` `snapToTerrain` spline sweeps your cambered kerbed `profile()`.
- An animal is yours to make: one `geometry(ctx)` with its `skeleton()`; `jiggle.bones` springs ears and tail; it bends as one skin `{ joints, weights }`; `ctx.bone(name)` binds a part turning whole. A CDN model (`cdn/model-red-fox.glb`, cooked from its name) is the road once the creator asks for a ready-made model again (their picture →uploaded-models). A model talks by its jaw or mouth key, never an added mouth. A humanoid (knight, guard, golem) is the art style's call: a CDN body playing library clips and holding what a new name says, or yours.
- A CROWD (fish, birds, leaves: dozens alike) is ONE instanced mesh, swayed by its `scripted` material's `positionNode`, no `skeleton()` per body. Thousands in ONE object are an instance set (`ctx.instances`).

Returns and the whole ctx: `spawn api GeometryContext`.
